declared_exclusions.item: Wildcard action expansion (e.g. 's3:*') into the concrete actions it covers
declared_exclusions.reason: Out of scope for AC1-AC5: a wildcard token in the granted set is carried VERBATIM and rendered unobservable, never silently dropped or falsely resolved against a specific tracked action. Expanding a wildcard into the full concrete action list a service exposes is a future refinement the cell does not require -- opal-data-refresh-lambda-role (AC2's test role) happens to carry no wildcard actions, so this path is exercised only by the offline self-test's 's3:*' fixture row, not by a live read.

declared_exclusions.item: AWS Access Analyzer (the access-analyzer:* unused-access finding type)
declared_exclusions.reason: C-ANALYZER-PRICED-FIRST bars it -- no per-role price has been read by anyone, and availability is not authorization. permission-cold uses IAM Access Advisor instead (free, core-IAM, iam:GenerateServiceLastAccessedDetails / iam:GetServiceLastAccessedDetails), the SAME API family role-cold already used for RoleLastUsedDate. Access Analyzer is never called anywhere in this extension.

declared_exclusions.item: (role, action, RESOURCE)-grain permission usage -- e.g. does this role use s3:GetObject on THIS bucket specifically vs any other
declared_exclusions.reason: IAM Access Advisor's ACTION_LEVEL granularity is (principal, action)-only, not resource-precise. comp-iam-usage's pre-existing reach-check already answers the resource-precise question for one NAMED (role, action, resource) triple via simulate-principal-policy; permission-cold answers the coarser question FWD-2 actually asks -- 'which of its granted permissions has this role never used' -- at the action grain, not the resource grain.
